title: Repair an API pagination helper
question:
A product API uses the pagination helper below, but customers report missing and overlapping results. Repair it.

Contract: solve(items, page, pageSize) returns {items, page, totalPages, hasNext, hasPrevious}. Pages are 1-based. Invalid or non-positive integer page values default to 1; invalid pageSize defaults to 10. A page beyond the final page returns an empty items list and preserves the requested page number. Empty input has zero totalPages. hasPrevious is true only when page > 1 and totalPages > 0.

Discuss the bug with your AI partner, make a focused change, and add a test that would have caught the original issue.

title: Process duplicate webhook deliveries
question:
Build an in-memory batch processor for payment events that may be retried. solve(events) returns {appliedIds, totals}.

Each valid event has a non-empty string id, a non-empty string account, and an integer amountCents (negative values are allowed). Skip malformed events, including null and non-object values. Boolean amounts are invalid. For duplicate IDs, apply only the first valid event; an invalid occurrence must not reserve its ID. Keep appliedIds in input order. totals maps each affected account to the sum of its applied amounts; keep zero totals.

Use your AI partner to design and implement the behavior. Explain which delivery guarantees this batch helper does and does not provide.

title: Refactor layered application settings
question:
Our shallow merge helper loses nested defaults. Refactor solve(defaults, overrides) into a predictable deep merge.

Both top-level inputs are JSON objects. Merge nested objects recursively. An override replaces a scalar, null, or array in full; arrays are never merged by index. Keep default properties that the override does not mention. Empty overrides preserve defaults. Do not mutate either input. You may assume no cycles and no special prototype keys.

title: Make a log summary resilient
question:
Fix the log summarizer so a malformed line does not break a whole dashboard. solve(lines) returns a list of {service, requests, errors, averageLatencyMs}, sorted by service name (ASCII ascending).

Each input line is a JSON string. A usable record is an object with a non-empty string service, a level in info/warn/error, and a finite, non-negative numeric latencyMs. Booleans are not valid latency values. Skip invalid JSON and invalid records. Count all usable records as requests and only error records as errors. Average latency uses all usable records for that service, rounded to the nearest integer using floor(mean + 0.5). Empty input returns [].

Use the partner to identify assumptions and repair the code, then explain the failures your tests cover.
sourceNotes: Original product-style practice task inspired by publicly described AI-assisted interview formats; not an employer question.
constraints: Implement solve(lines). All inputs and outputs are JSON-compatible.

starterCodes.python:
import json

def solve(lines):
    records = [json.loads(line) for line in lines]
    return [{"service": r["service"], "requests": 1, "errors": 0, "averageLatencyMs": r["latencyMs"]} for r in records]

title: Add a capped retry schedule
question:
Implement a deterministic retry helper for a background worker. solve(attempts, baseDelayMs, maxDelayMs) returns the delay for each retry, with attempt zero using baseDelayMs. Each later delay doubles, capped at maxDelayMs. If baseDelayMs exceeds the cap, the first retry is already capped. Zero attempts returns [].

Inputs are non-negative integers, attempts <= 30, and delays <= 1,000,000. This task has no jitter and never sleeps. Discuss with your partner how jitter and retryable error classification would fit into a real worker, but keep them out of this function.
